hebrews.1.p1.b2.text: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.

hebrews.1.p1.b3.text: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.

hebrews.1.p2.b4.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word.

hebrews.1.p2.b5.text: After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

hebrews.1.p3.b6.text: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father”? …

hebrews.1.p3.b7.text: Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son”?

hebrews.1.p3.b8.text: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.” … “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”

hebrews.1.p4.b9.text: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

hebrews.1.p4.b10.text: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

hebrews.1.p4.b11.text: … they will all wear out like a garment. … You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed …

hebrews.1.p4.b12.text: … but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.

hebrews.1.p5.b13.text: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet”?

hebrews.1.p5.b14.text: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?
